description: Explosion at Kīlauea summit, ~6 pm HST 24 May 2018; 'produced an ash cloud that rose to 10,000 feet above sea level' (USGS). Real-time ground shot of a cauliflower grey ash cloud boiling up from the crater, dark ash drifting up-right under an overcast evening sky. Small 'USGS' bug at bottom-left (keep or crop). Best available real explosive-ash footage; it is a small phreatic explosion, not Plinian – use as generic 'ash cloud' b-roll.
